comment: The table of the gate of the oracle test (test/fort/owner/oracle_test.ft) and of its
disposition table (test/fort/support/disposition.ft). The gate fails an item when a run
gives an error event that no rule of the compiler for that item excuses (D17.11, D17.20,
D17.21). A row mutes one error kind, or changes when a `leak` or a `leak at exit` is an
error. Other rows break the order of the table, change a count, a family or a kind of
KNOWN, or raise a row of FLOORS. Other rows give each item of one family an error, or
take a rule from an item. Other rows let a report line excuse an event of another rule.
One row takes each row of FORCED from the case that only FORCED runs. The sources are
test sources and no part of the compiler binary. So the build writes both into one file,
and the md5 guard reads that file. The stage runs the oracle test, which compiles the two
A row counts as caught only when the test stops with a panic of the gate: the pinned
stdout of the test alone holds no row. The table runs in the Linux VM with the debug
preset and the default runner after `tools/vm build`.

stages.name: the oracle test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/oracle_test
